content: The progress, milestones, and lessons learned from the implementation of national One Health initiatives to date should be summarized. This includes a detailed analysis of existing mechanisms, strategies, plans, frameworks, and activities, which should be covered in the situation analysis section. A downloadable template for the national One Health action plan and its associated workplan is available, tailored to country-specific needs, as provided by WHO in 2023. The purpose of the national One Health action plan is to either strengthen an existing plan or develop a new one in alignment with the One Health Joint Plan of Action (OH JPA). This plan should integrate and build upon existing One Health-related efforts. It should also outline the scope of implementation from national to subnational levels and define the timeframes for execution. The alignment of this plan with the global Quadripartite OH JPA should be clearly described. The process for sharing outcomes, outputs, and lessons learned from national One Health implementation with other stakeholders should be detailed as a cross-cutting activity. This ensures that knowledge and experiences are disseminated effectively. In Stage 1, a situation analysis should be conducted. This includes stakeholder mapping and analysis, with a description of the approach and results. A review of national One Health governance and coordination should be performed, including a SWOT (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats) analysis. Additionally, completed assessments related to One Health should be reviewed, identifying gaps, how they have been addressed, and plans for future assessments. If no recent assessments have been conducted, a One Health assessment should be carried out using existing tools. Existing national action plans, strategies, frameworks, and activities related to One Health should be identified and described. This should include an analysis of alignment with the six action tracks of the OH JPA and identification of any gaps. In Stage 2, the establishment or strengthening of a multisectoral One Health coordination mechanism is essential. This mechanism should include details on when and how it was established, the sectors represented, and its whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach. Gender equity should be reflected in the mechanism, and gender sensitivity should be applied in all aspects of its governance. Supporting policies and legislation for institutionalization and sustainability should be described, along with any associated technical advisory or working groups, challenges, and lessons learned. For countries without such a mechanism, it is critical to establish one before proceeding to the next stage of implementation planning. In Stage 3, planning for implementation involves prioritizing activities. The approach and results of prioritizing action tracks and pathways of change from the OH JPA should be described, tailored to the country’s needs and context. The findings from the Stage 1 situation analysis should serve as the basis for prioritization. Strategic objectives and outcomes for the national One Health action plan should be listed in alignment with the OH JPA. A workplan and budget should be developed, and a monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) framework should be included, using the associated national One Health workplan Excel template. Resource mobilization for sustainable funding and institutionalization of the national One Health action plan should be described. This includes domestic and international financing, as well as any return on investment, economic analysis, or investment planning for One Health interventions in the country. Contact information for the focal points or offices responsible for implementing and monitoring the national One Health action plan should be provided. Relevant references, such as existing national action plans and assessment reports cited in the document, should also be listed. Annex 2 provides a link to the One Health High-Level Expert Panel (OHHLEP) inventory of One Health tools and resources. These resources can assist countries in identifying tools to incorporate into national One Health action plans, as well as completed One Health-related assessments to inform priorities for implementation. They can also support the establishment or strengthening of One Health mechanisms.
